title: Keep T1 MacBook Pros in S3 instead of an Alpine Ridge wake loop
author: ijt
body:
Fixes https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/12194

## Why

On MacBookPro14,2 (2017 13\", T1, no T2 chip) the two JHL6540 Alpine Ridge Thunderbolt 3 controllers emit PME about every 45s and pull the machine out of `deep` S3 with the lid still closed. logind sees the closed lid and suspends again. That loop ran for hours here: the chassis got hot in a bag, and after enough cycles thunderbolt resume hung (`tb_cfg_read/write: -108`, `pcieport … D3cold to D0, device inaccessible`). Opening the lid did nothing; only a power-button hold recovered it.

`install/hardware/apple/fix-suspend-nvme.sh` already matches these DMI ids. T2 setup correctly no-ops (`106b:180[12]` is absent). This is the missing T1 half.

## What

Gated on `MacBookPro13,[123]|MacBookPro14,[123]`:

- Disable ACPI wakeup on RP05/RP09/XHC2/XHC3 (TB) and RP12 (Wi-Fi PME). LID0 and SPIT stay enabled.
- udev: `8086:15d2` / `8086:15d4` `power/wakeup=disabled`.
- Limine drop-in `pcie_port_pm=off` so those ports do not sit in D3 for ~1s each on resume.
- Oneshoot at boot reapplies the ACPI toggles (they reset).
- Migration sources the same installer leaf (no-op on any other machine).

## Explicitly not in this PR

- **Not** `pm_async=off`. That is correct on some T2 boxes and wrong here: it serialized the D3 waits into a ~60s black screen.
- **Not** `blacklist thunderbolt`. USB-C charging still works without the module; docks / DP-alt would not. Wakeup disable + `pcie_port_pm=off` is the conservative first patch.
- **Not** switching to s2idle. S3 works on this firmware; s2idle is the heat path.

## Test plan

- On MacBookPro14,2 / 13,x: close lid, leave closed. Journal should show one `PM: suspend entry (deep)` and no wake until lid open. Machine stays cool.
- Open lid: resume to the lock screen.
- Other hardware: installer/migration no-op.
- `./test/cli` and `test/shell.d/alpine-ridge-suspend-test.sh`.

Proven on Omarchy 4.0.2-1, MacBookPro14,2, kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2. After these local equivalents, a 30-minute lid-closed stretch came back immediately and was cool to the touch.

Sibling: lid-close debounce in https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12210 (#12193).

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# omarchy:summary=Disable Alpine Ridge Thunderbolt wakeup from S3
+# omarchy:group=hw
+# omarchy:hidden=true
+# omarchy:requires-sudo=true
+
+# Alpine Ridge NHIs emit PME about every 45s and pull T1 MacBooks out of deep
+# sleep with the lid still closed. logind then suspends again. That loop is the
+# heat, and after enough cycles resume hangs.
+#
+# Toggle /proc/acpi/wakeup only while a node is currently enabled. LID0 and
+# SPIT stay enabled so the lid and keyboard can still wake the machine.
+
+wakeup_file=${OMARCHY_ACPI_WAKEUP:-/proc/acpi/wakeup}
+
+[[ -w $wakeup_file || -f $wakeup_file ]] || exit 0
+
+for dev in RP05 RP09 XHC2 XHC3 RP12; do
+  if grep -Eq "^${dev}[[:space:]].*enabled" "$wakeup_file"; then
+    printf '%s\n' "$dev" > "$wakeup_file"
+  fi
+done

@@ -0,0 +1,58 @@
+# Stop Intel Alpine Ridge Thunderbolt 3 from waking 2016–2017 MacBook Pros
+# out of S3. These machines are T1 (no T2 chip). Keep deep sleep; s2idle is
+# the heat path. Do not set pm_async=off (that serializes D3 timeouts into a
+# minute-long black screen) and do not blacklist thunderbolt (USB-C docks).
+
+MACBOOK_MODEL=$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/product_name 2>/dev/null || true)
+
+if [[ ! $MACBOOK_MODEL =~ MacBookPro13,[123]|MacBookPro14,[123] ]]; then
+  return 0 2>/dev/null || exit 0
+fi
+
+echo "Detected $MACBOOK_MODEL; disabling Alpine Ridge S3 wakeup"
+
+udev_rules=/etc/udev/rules.d/99-omarchy-alpine-ridge-wakeup.rules
+limine_conf=/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/alpine-ridge-suspend.conf
+service=/etc/systemd/system/omarchy-alpine-ridge-wakeup.service
+
+sudo mkdir -p /etc/udev/rules.d /etc/limine-entry-tool.d /etc/systemd/system /etc/omarchy
+
+# S3 resume on these parts is ~7s, so lid-close waits 20s (see
+# omarchy-system-lid-suspend) instead of the 3s default. Leave an admin-set
+# value alone.
+if [[ ! -f /etc/omarchy/lid-suspend-delay ]]; then
+  printf '20\n' | sudo tee /etc/omarchy/lid-suspend-delay >/dev/null
+fi
+
+sudo tee "$udev_rules" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
+# Alpine Ridge NHI (8086:15d2) and xHCI (8086:15d4) must not wake S3.
+ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="pci", ATTR{vendor}=="0x8086", ATTR{device}=="0x15d2", ATTR{power/wakeup}="disabled"
+ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="pci", ATTR{vendor}=="0x8086", ATTR{device}=="0x15d4", ATTR{power/wakeup}="disabled"
+EOF
+
+sudo tee "$limine_conf" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
+# Alpine Ridge ports do not return from D3; skip PCIe port power management.
+KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" pcie_port_pm=off"
+EOF
+
+sudo tee "$service" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
+[Unit]
+Description=Disable Alpine Ridge Thunderbolt wakeup from S3
+After=sysinit.target
+
+[Service]
+Type=oneshot
+RemainAfterExit=yes
+ExecStart=/usr/bin/omarchy-hw-alpine-ridge-wakeup
+
+[Install]
+WantedBy=multi-user.target
+EOF
+
+sudo systemctl enable --now omarchy-alpine-ridge-wakeup.service
+
+if ! grep -Eq '(^| )pcie_port_pm=off( |$)' /proc/cmdline 2>/dev/null; then
+  if command -v limine-mkinitcpio >/dev/null; then
+    sudo limine-mkinitcpio
+  fi
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+echo "Stop Alpine Ridge Thunderbolt from waking T1 MacBooks out of S3"
+
+fix="$OMARCHY_PATH/install/hardware/apple/fix-suspend-alpine-ridge.sh"
+[[ -f $fix ]] || exit 0
+
+# The installer leaf is meant to be sourced; it returns when the DMI id does
+# not match so a migration on any other machine is a no-op.
+source "$fix"

@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+fix="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-suspend-alpine-ridge.sh"
+wakeup="$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hw-alpine-ridge-wakeup"
+all="$ROOT/install/hardware/all.sh"
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1789604768.sh"
+
+grep -F 'MacBookPro13,[123]|MacBookPro14,[123]' "$fix" >/dev/null
+grep -F 'pcie_port_pm=off' "$fix" >/dev/null
+grep -F '/etc/omarchy/lid-suspend-delay' "$fix" >/dev/null
+grep -F '20' "$fix" >/dev/null
+grep -F '8086:15d2' "$fix" >/dev/null
+grep -F '8086:15d4' "$fix" >/dev/null
+! grep -E '^[^#]*pm_async=off' "$fix" >/dev/null ||
+  fail "Alpine Ridge setup does not set pm_async=off"
+! grep -E '^[^#]*blacklist thunderbolt' "$fix" >/dev/null ||
+  fail "Alpine Ridge setup does not blacklist thunderbolt"
+pass "Alpine Ridge setup keeps deep S3 and Thunderbolt loaded"
+
+grep -F 'fix-suspend-alpine-ridge.sh' "$all" >/dev/null
+pass "hardware install runs the Alpine Ridge suspend fix"
+
+grep -F 'RP05 RP09 XHC2 XHC3 RP12' "$wakeup" >/dev/null
+! grep -E '^[^#]*LID0' "$wakeup" >/dev/null || fail "lid wake stays enabled"
+! grep -E '^[^#]*SPIT' "$wakeup" >/dev/null || fail "keyboard wake stays enabled"
+pass "Alpine Ridge wakeup disables TB and Wi-Fi PME only"
+
+grep -F 'source "$fix"' "$migration" >/dev/null
+pass "migration reapplies the Alpine Ridge suspend fix"
+
+tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT
+wakeup_file="$tmpdir/wakeup"
+cat >"$wakeup_file" <<'EOF'
+RP05	S3	*enabled   pci:0000:00:1c.4
+LID0	S4	*enabled   platform:PNP0C0D:00
+SPIT	S3	*enabled   spi:spi-APP000D:00
+EOF
+
+OMARCHY_ACPI_WAKEUP="$wakeup_file" "$wakeup"
+[[ $(<"$wakeup_file") == RP05 ]] ||
+  fail "wakeup helper toggles an enabled TB node" "got: $(<"$wakeup_file")"
+pass "wakeup helper toggles an enabled TB node"

comments.body: Follow-up: the installer also writes `/etc/omarchy/lid-suspend-delay` with `20` on these DMI ids (leaves an existing value alone). That pairs with #12210, which reads the file and also keys the same 20s delay off DMI so T1 Macs get it even before this hardware leaf runs.
